title: FOSFOMYCIN AS AN ORAL ALTERNATIVE THERAPY IN THE TREATMENT OF ACUTE BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS CAUSED BY MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT ESCHERICHIA COLI. PILOT STUDY
official: FOSFOMYCIN AS AN ORAL ALTERNATIVE THERAPY IN THE TREATMENT OF ACUTE BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS CAUSED BY MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT ESCHERICHIA COLI. PILOT STUDY
summary: Main objective: Phase IV, prospective, interventional clinical trial to demonstrate the efficacy of oral fosfomycin-tromethamol in the treatment of acute multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli bacterial prostatitis compared to a prospective control group of sensitive E. coli BAP treated with approved therapeutic alternatives.
conditions: Prostatitis aguda bacteriana (PAB) por Escherichia coli multirresitente.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Casos: varones de 18 años o más con prostatitis aguda bacteriana con un urinocultivo y/o hemocultivo positivo por E. coli tratados con fosfomicina vía oral. Controles: varones de 18 años o más con prostatitis aguda bacteriana con urinocultivo o hemocultivos positivo por E. coli E. coli tratados con terapia convencional (ciprofloxacino o cotrimoxazol)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known allergy or intolerance to fosfomycin
2. Polycystic kidney disease
3. History of known chronic prostatitis
4. Patient with 2 or more episodes of PAB in the previous year or 1 episode in the last 6 months
5. Immunocompromised patients (kidney transplant recipients, liver cirrhosis, patients on renal replacement therapy, chronic treatment with corticosteroids, receiving active chemotherapy, use of anti-TNF)
6. Terminal situation or estimated life expectancy of less than 90 days or in purely palliative treatment for their underlying illness
7. Patients who are participating in another clinical trial with active treatment
8. MIC to fosfomycin higher than that established by the study inclusion criteria.
9. Patients who refuse to give consent to participate in the study.
10. Polymicrobial bacteremia or urine culture
11. Clinical criteria for acute pyelonephritis (positive fist-kidney percussion, urinary tract obstruction, kidney abscess).
12. Anatomical alterations of the urinary tract
13. Urinary infections associated with urinary catheters
14. Undrained prostatic abscess
15. Other concomitant infection
16. Patients who have not achieved clinical stability after 5 days of parenteral treatment
17. Patients with septic shock at the time of randomization
